issues.description: Default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silent breaking change for existing integrations
issues.detail: The default turn_detection_mode flips from EXTERNAL to FIXED. Existing pipelines relying on Pipecat's built-in endpointing via UserStoppedSpeakingFrame will silently change behavior because the handler now listens for VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame instead. The changelog notes it but a migration note and deprecation warning would respect the reader.

issues.description: _enable_vad invariant is not stated and its truth table is non-obvious
issues.detail: The predicate `end_of_utterance_mode not in [FIXED, EXTERNAL]` controls both frame emission and finalization routing. There is no comment stating the invariant: VAD-enabled means engine owns endpointing, VAD-disabled means Pipecat owns it. A reader auditing this file must reconstruct the table from scattered call sites. One literate comment near the assignment would fix it.

issues.description: Warning-then-no-op branch when VAD frame arrives with internal VAD enabled is dead code by construction
issues.detail: If internal VAD is enabled, upstream should not be emitting VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame to this processor. The warning fires but nothing is finalized, leaving the user wondering what happened. Either route the frame defensively (call finalize anyway) or state explicitly in a comment why the no-op is correct. Right now the branch is a footgun without an invariant.

issues.description: speech_segment_config is unconditionally overwritten, discarding any prior assignment
issues.detail: `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=...)` replaces the whole object. If a future field is added to SpeechSegmentConfig or set elsewhere in _prepare_config, it is silently clobbered. Prefer mutating the existing config or constructing once with all known fields. Small now, interest-bearing later.

issues.description: split_sentences docstring omits interaction with turn detection and diarization
issues.detail: The docstring says sentences are emitted as finals mid-turn but does not specify whether they participate in turn boundaries, how they interleave with speaker changes, or what downstream sees for ordering. A reader has to run the code to know. A one-paragraph literate comment with a worked example would suffice.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics call was moved rather than resolved
issues.detail: The line `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` was relocated from after the broadcast to before it. Commented code with no explanation is noise; either delete it or land it with a comment stating why it is disabled and under what condition it should be re-enabled. The move makes the diff harder to read for no gain.

review.summary: The change is small and largely correct, but it ships a silent default-behavior flip (EXTERNAL to FIXED) coupled with a change in which frame triggers finalization (UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame). The central _enable_vad invariant governing this routing is not stated in a comment, and the warn-but-do-nothing branch when a VAD frame arrives under internal VAD is a latent footgun. The SpeechSegmentConfig assignment overwrites rather than mutates, which is fine today and interest-bearing tomorrow. UNDER-AUDITED on the invariant; NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on split_sentences and the VAD truth table.
